correctness.rationale: For all integers n≥2, Clebsch–Gordan fusion and orthogonality yield the complete seven exact mixed sixth moments and S_n=(n³+3n²+4n+2)/2. Termwise nonnegative invariant multiplicities imply sharp complex phase alignment; positive mixed coefficients determine all allowed equality phases. Even n reduce to an exact cubic with a Bernstein-form derivative strictly positive for n≥6 and one interior critical point for n=2,4. Odd n reduce to a sixth-degree polynomial whose derivative numerator has exactly one positive zero by Descartes and endpoint signs, with t_n~5/(2n). The analytic proof establishes the universal claim; standalone checker independently obtained 4,724 finite assertions via representation convolution and semicircle Chebyshev integration. Scientific limits: n≥2, precisely two central characters, sixth moment only.

value.rationale: A natural SU2 central Fourier two-mode packet has an infinite-weight family of exactly determined sharp sixth norms and all complex equality cases. The even-versus-odd bifurcation is qualitative: for n even≥6 the smaller mode is rigorously absent from the optimizer; for every odd n it contributes positively, with an explicit asymptotic ratio and gain. These contrasts are not evident from character orthogonality or generic sharp norm estimates, and they supply a complete sharp all-weight classification rather than an isolated small-n example.
